name: Transition Difficulty
summary: Distress or resistance when moving from one activity, place, or routine to another — driven by a need for predictability and difficulty anticipating what comes next, not simple stubbornness.
triggers: Unexpected or abrupt changes with no warning
Not knowing what will happen next or how long it will last
Being interrupted mid-activity, especially a preferred one
Multiple transitions packed close together with little recovery time
Sensory or environmental differences between the two settings

remedies.text: Visual schedules showing the sequence of activities so the person can see what's coming and mentally prepare
Advance verbal or visual warnings before a transition ('5 more minutes, then we clean up') rather than a sudden stop
Social stories that walk through a specific upcoming change in simple, concrete language
A consistent transition object, song, or ritual that signals 'it's time to switch' across settings

sources.label: Indiana Resource Center for Autism - Transition Time: Helping Individuals on the Autism Spectrum Move Successfully from One Activity to Another
Autism Speaks - Visual Supports and Autism Spectrum Disorder
